failure_summary.description: The assistant proposed a named area and the user said 'Yes' or 'What's there?'. The agent used city= (T2), re-ran search_attractions (T6), or re-passed the previous turn's budget (T8) instead of neighborhood=[area].

A date or date-range reply produced only part of the required searches. T5 dropped the hotel that had a stay length ('4 nights'). T7 produced one flight leg and omitted the stated class 'first'. Rule 9's 'Add no other params: no flight_class' contradicts the stated-class-goes-into-search rule.

T1 applied a hotel-amenity 'Yes' as a filter on the cached attractions key, when no hotels key existed and the dates were missing, so only seek_information was correct. T3 re-filtered the flight keys on a hotel reply and dropped the neighborhood.
T4 emitted a bare search_hotels call with no assignment or save, plus a stray </parameter> tag, which caused a SyntaxError. Existing hygiene rules already cover this.

patch.reasoning: The meta-skill says to avoid new gates and instead de-conflict and make small amendments inside the rule that owns each decision. Four edits do this. (1) The assistant-proposed-area reply caused 3 of 8 failures. I generalize the existing SEARCH GATE example in place so it covers all cached domains and the phrasings 'Yes', 'X would be great' and 'What's there?'. It forces neighborhood=[area] only and rules out city=, re-search, and re-passed earlier kwargs. (2) Rule 9 says 'Add no other params: no flight_class', which contradicts the stated-class-goes-into-both-legs rule and likely caused T7's missing class. I remove the contradiction. (3) The DATE ANSWER rule gets one sentence so a single date plus a stay length still yields the hotel via adjust_date, which fixes T5 where the hotel was dropped. (4) The DATE GATE sentence about hotel replies gets an extension so a hotel-amenity 'Yes' with no hotels key and no dates produces only seek_information instead of a filter on another domain's key, which fixes T1. No sections are added and no earlier rejected edit is repeated.

edits.target: attractions cached + a neighborhood the assistant proposed
edits.content: an area the assistant proposed ('Have you considered 4th Avenue?', 'Are you looking at Downtown Raleigh?') answered by 'Yes', 'Yeah, Downtown Raleigh would be great' or 'No, I haven't. What's there?' on whichever cached domain is being discussed (restaurants, hotels or attractions) uses ONLY neighborhood=["<area exactly as the assistant wrote it>"]: never city=, never a new search_*, never the budget, rating or type of an earlier turn. Example: attractions cached + the proposed area

edits.target: Add no other params: no airline, flight_class, budget, times or num_people.
edits.content: Add only params the user stated anywhere in the conversation: a stated flight_class or airline goes into BOTH legs ('first' in turn 1 -> flight_class=["first"] on departure_flights and return_flights). Never invent an airline, budget, times or num_people.

edits.target: Never load another domain's key and re-save it as a stand-in for the missing search.
edits.content: Never load another domain's key and re-save it as a stand-in for the missing search. A reply with ONE date plus a stay length ('4 nights') also completes the hotel: `checkout_date = adjust_date(date="<X>", delta_days=4)`, then search_hotels with checkin_date=["<X>"] and checkout_date=[checkout_date] in the same block, after the flight search. 'Weekend getaway' is context and does not cancel the hotel.

edits.target: reply 'around 80 per night' -> seek_information, no search_hotels).
edits.content: reply 'around 80 per night' -> seek_information, no search_hotels). The same holds for 'Yes, we need a pool and room service' when CACHE has no hotels key and no dates are known: the whole output is the one seek_information for the dates, never a filter on 'attractions', 'restaurants' or a flight key.
